checked_equations: L={S⊆V: every four-set contained in S induces a connected graph}
correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the ordinary four-cut definition from complements of disconnected induced 4-subgraphs on the 15 two-subsets of [6]. Exact Alexander dual L forbids all disconnected 4-subsets, including larger faces; its face counts by size 0..7 are (1,15,105,455,750,492,70,0). A verified staged vertex-toggle matching on all 1,887 nonempty dual faces pairs 925 covers and leaves one critical 0-cell plus 36 critical 4-cells; the full 7,455-cover oriented Hasse digraph is acyclic by a topological sort of all 1,887 faces. Forman gives L≃ wedge^36 S4. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality for 15 vertices gives reduced H8(K,Z)=Z^36 and all other reduced integral homology zero. Independently enumerated K has 615 10-facets and the complete seven-skeleton, hence is six-connected; H7=0 and Hurewicz give seven-connectivity, and representatives of the H8 basis yield wedge^36 S8 via homological Whitehead. Pure ten-dimensional K has nonzero lower-degree homology and is not shellable.
risks: The full finite certificate establishes this fixed graph only, not a general infinite Kneser family.
No equivariant homotopy claim or formal proof-assistant attestation.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original exact nonequivariant homotopy classification for the ordinary 4-cut complex of KG(6,2). The strongest same-definition Kneser result in the primary 2024 paper is an ordinary 2-cut theorem in a triangle-free range; the 2025 sequel treats disjoint unions, squared paths and grids; published same-graph Čech and equal-numerical Heawood results concern different simplicial complexes. Resultary high-girth general theorem is inapplicable because this graph has triangles. No searched equivalent or logically stronger statement was found, with an explicit risk of an unindexed equivalent computation.

value.rationale: KG(6,2) is the canonical first triangle-containing two-subset Kneser graph immediately after the Petersen graph KG(5,2); it is a natural boundary beyond the triangle-free two-cut result in the main literature. The ordinary four-cut construction is a standard graph complex invariant, and a complete integral homotopy type at this natural graph/cut parameter can be useful independently of an all-Kneser classification. The 36 eight-spheres arise two dimensions below its pure ten-dimensional facets, proving an informative nonshellability obstruction that cannot be read from the facet count or Euler characteristic alone. The certified homotopy classification uses a nontrivial acyclic matching and Alexander duality, not a textbook substitution or an arbitrary numerical slice. Its scope is explicitly one finite, nonequivariant graph and it does not assert broader families.
